title: Website Maintenance vs Redesign: Fix It or Start Over?
h1: Website maintenance vs redesign: fix it or start over?
description: How to decide whether your website needs maintenance, targeted fixes or a full redesign, with signs to look for, what each involves and who to hire.
intro: When a website starts to feel slow, dated or hard to manage, many owners jump straight to a full redesign. Sometimes that is the right call. Often, though, the site needs updates, fixes and a few focused improvements rather than a rebuild. Choosing wrongly either wastes money on a new site that repeats old problems or keeps you patching a site that should have been replaced. This article helps you tell the difference.

faq.q: How often does a website need maintenance?
faq.a: Updates and backups should happen regularly, often monthly, with security checks in between.

faq.q: Will a redesign improve my search rankings?
faq.a: Not automatically. A careless redesign can even lose rankings if pages and redirects are not handled.

faq.q: Can I redesign without changing platforms?
faq.a: Yes. Many redesigns keep the same platform and change the design and content.

faq.q: What should a maintenance plan include?
faq.a: Updates, backups, security monitoring, uptime checks and a set amount of small changes.

faq.q: How do I know if my site is too old?
faq.a: If basic updates are impossible or every change breaks something, a rebuild is often cheaper long term.
